To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) graph-based relational models are a strong inductive prior for source code; 2) hybrid models that combine the global nature of Transformers with the relational inductive bias of graph-based models outperform both graph-only and Transformer-only models; 3) the proposed GREAT model is the best-performing model for the variable misuse task; and 4) the proposed Graph Sandwich model is the best performing model for the variable usage task.

(i) Graph Sandwiches are a new model family that can improve upon traditional graph-based models by up to 15% on the variable-misuse prediction task, and (ii) Graph Relational Embeddings are a new model component that can improve upon the state-of-the-art by 10-15% on the same task, while using fewer parameters and training faster than the state-of-theart.
